# Run comparison view in the Dashboard (side-by-side and diff)

## Description

Delivers the core experiment-comparison capability in the RHOAI Dashboard:
users select two or more training and/or pipeline runs and see their parameters
and metrics side by side, with diff highlighting between two selected runs.
Today, parameters and metrics are visible only on individual per-run pages, so
comparison happens in exported spreadsheets; this epic makes comparison a
first-class, in-platform workflow starting from the runs list.

## Scope

- Multi-selection of two or more runs (training runs and Data Science
  Pipelines runs) from the runs list in the Dashboard.
- A comparison view presenting the parameters and metrics of all selected runs
  side by side.
- Diff presentation for two selected runs: parameters and metrics whose values
  differ between the two runs are highlighted.
- The comparison view consumes run parameters and metrics exactly as they
  exist today — the same data the per-run pages show; no change to how runs or
  their metadata are stored or produced.
- Respects the strategy's out-of-scope boundaries: no automatic best-run
  selection or promotion, and no comparison across clusters or across projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given two or more runs in a project, When the user selects them from the
   runs list and opens the comparison, Then the parameters and metrics of every
   selected run are displayed side by side. (HLR-1)
2. Given exactly two selected runs, When the comparison is displayed, Then the
   parameters and metrics whose values differ between the two runs are visually
   distinguished from those that are identical. (HLR-3)
3. Given runs produced through Data Science Pipelines, When they are included
   in a comparison, Then their existing parameters and metrics render correctly
   in the comparison view and the existing per-run pages are unaffected.
   (passive validation of Data Science Pipelines — no pipeline-side change)
4. Given runs that live in different projects, When the user attempts a
   comparison, Then they cannot be combined into a single comparison
   (comparison is scoped within one project). (out-of-scope boundary)
5. The Dashboard's existing build and test pipelines remain green with these
   changes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — "Users can select two or more runs and view their
  parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard": fully covered by this
  epic.
- **HLR-3 (P1)** — "Provide a run 'diff' view that highlights which parameters
  and metrics changed between two selected runs": covered by this epic. HLR-1
  and HLR-3 describe the same comparison surface (the strategy notes overlapping
  wording from consolidated customer councils), so they are implemented together
  in one epic rather than building the same UI surface, selection model, and
  data access twice.

# Producing-run lineage on registered model versions

## Description

Makes a registered model version carry a reference to the run that produced
it, exposed through the Model Registry's REST API, so that platform clients
and the registry UI can resolve the experiment lineage behind a model version.
This is the data foundation that allows a run comparison to be opened from the
Model Registry and gives model promotion decisions visibility into what
produced each candidate version.

## Scope

- Record, on registered model versions, a reference to the run that produced
  them, using the registry's existing model-version metadata extension point
  (custom properties on model versions are the documented extension mechanism
  for attaching structured metadata).
- Expose the producing-run reference through the Model Registry REST API
  (OpenAPI-specified) so clients can read it for any model version.
- Additive and backward compatible: model versions registered without a
  producing run are unaffected, and existing registration, versioning, and
  artifact catalog behavior is unchanged.
- The reference is populated through the registry's existing registration
  interfaces; this epic introduces no new registration flow.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a model version registered with a producing run, When the model
   version is read through the Model Registry REST API, Then the run that
   produced it is identifiable from the version's metadata. (HLR-2)
2. Given a model version with no producing-run reference, When the version is
   read or listed, Then registry behavior is unchanged from today (the linkage
   is optional and additive).
3. Given the producing-run reference on a model version, When it is consumed
   by a client, Then it identifies the run sufficiently to locate that run
   within its project.
4. The Model Registry's existing build and test pipelines remain green with
   these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)** — "Registered model versions link back to the run that
  produced them": this epic delivers the lineage data on model versions and
  its API exposure (the registry-side half of the requirement; the registry UI
  entry point that consumes it is delivered by separate Dashboard work).

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry

## Description

Adds the Model Registry entry point to the run comparison capability: from a
registered model version in the Dashboard's Model Registry UI, a user can open
a run comparison that includes the run which produced that version. This closes
the loop between model promotion decisions and the experiments behind them —
a user reviewing registered versions can jump straight into comparing the runs
that produced them.

## Scope

- In the Dashboard's Model Registry UI, surface the producing-run reference
  carried on a registered model version.
- Provide an action from a registered model version that opens the run
  comparison view with the linked run included among the compared runs.
- Handle model versions that carry no producing-run reference gracefully (no
  broken entry point).
- Consume the producing-run reference as exposed by the Model Registry; this
  epic makes no change to Model Registry data or API.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a registered model version that references a producing run, When the
   user opens a comparison from the Model Registry UI, Then the run comparison
   view opens with that run included among the compared runs. (HLR-2)
2. Given a registered model version with no producing-run reference, When the
   version is viewed in the registry UI, Then no broken comparison entry point
   is presented (the entry is absent or inert rather than erroring).
3. The Dashboard's existing build and test pipelines remain green with these
   changes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)** — "so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry":
  this epic delivers the registry UI entry point (the lineage data it reads is
  delivered by the registry-side work on model versions).

   feature.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9015: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs

Triage outcome: full decomposition. The strategy is not below-threshold (it spans
multiple components — Dashboard, Model Registry, Data Science Pipelines — and
multiple teams, so the single-component/single-team conditions fail), and it is
not docs-only (code changes are required in the Dashboard and the Model
Registry). The strategy declares no open questions, no conditional ADRs, no
pending reviews, and no external dependencies, so no Investigation epics are
needed. All affected components exist in the platform (architecture context
files present, Konflux-onboarded), so no onboarding chain is required.

| Dashboard | Dashboard | yes (GA) | Active — new comparison UI | E001, E003 | RHOAI Dashboard |

Notes:

- All strategy component names match canonical names in `.context/rhai-components.txt` exactly; no non-obvious mappings were needed.

The strategy does not assign this validation to the RHOAI Pipelines team; if that team must own it, a small validation epic should be carved out (see Health Warnings).

    E002["E002 — Run lineage on model versions"] --> E003

| E001 → E003 | Rule 12 (framework → consumer) | The registry entry point navigates to the run comparison view; it is a consumer of that surface and cannot be built before the view exists. |

| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 | Same. |

| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. | E001 |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

**Redundancy note (HLR-1 / HLR-3).** The strategy states its requirements were
consolidated from two customer councils and that overlapping wording was kept.
HLR-1 (side-by-side view of parameters and metrics for two or more runs) and
HLR-3 (diff highlighting of changed parameters and metrics between two selected

and the same multi-select interaction. Per the priority-split rule, a
lower-priority HLR that is tightly coupled to the same implementation surface is
kept bundled: both map to E001. Splitting them would force two epics to build
the same UI surface, selection model, and data access independently. E001's
priority is P0, the highest priority of its mapped HLRs.

**Priority derivation.** E001 = P0 (HLR-1). E002 and E003 = P1 (HLR-2). E004
uses the docs-authoring priority exception: the strategy frontmatter priority is
`Major`, which maps to P1 (HLR-4's P2 label does not propagate, and docs edges
do not trigger priority inheritance). No priority inversion exists: no P0 work
is blocked by P1 work — E001 has no dependencies and delivers the strategy's
P0 value on its own.

1. **HLR-1/HLR-3 redundancy** — see the traceability note above. The two HLRs
   overlap in wording and surface; they are deliberately bundled into the P0
   comparison epic. If the diff view is intended as a separately scheduled
   deliverable, it must be re-planned explicitly rather than emerging from an
   accidental epic split.
2. **Missing strategy sections** — the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
   Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no
   non-functional requirements; Affected Components is a bare list without
   what-changes/owner columns. Teams were derived from architecture context
   owning teams and acceptance criteria were derived from the HLRs.
3. **Documentation owner assumed** — HLR-4 implies documentation work but the
   strategy names no owner; E004 is assigned to the Documentation component /
   RHOAI Documentation team. Verify the owning team before scheduling.
4. **Passive-component validation ownership** — Data Science Pipelines
   validation is folded into E001 as an acceptance criterion, executed from the
   Dashboard side (which reads the run data). If the RHOAI Pipelines team is
   expected to own that validation, a separate small validation epic owned by
   that team should be carved out.
5. **No scope traps detected** — the out-of-scope items (automatic best-run
   selection or promotion; comparison across clusters or across projects) are
   respected as boundary acceptance criteria and do not contradict any stated
   NFR (none exist).
